entry_state: Capped participation requires recalculating ordinary attribution after each assumed share issue. A restricted ordering result survives fixed rights and independent nonnegative gross effects. Joint bonus or tax consequences can violate that additivity; a two-convertible bonus-threshold example now begins.
exit_state: Joint conversion changes the threshold bonus and tax, so isolated earnings increments need not add. The four hypothetical worlds remain calculable while final nonadditive selection is unevaluated. Contingent options also require the stated similar-instrument prerequisite. A separate participating-dividend case now introduces a hypothetical tax benefit allocated to ordinary holders.
findings: The P90 case produces joint earnings92 rather than96 from isolated addbacks. P80 has individually antidilutive conversions but a lower combined EPS, without establishing admissible selection.
The text distinguishes the fixed-effect official example from the unaddressed shared-threshold case and does not infer a general ranking policy.
